correctness.rationale: In a triangle-free cubic prism a connected seed of three vertices forms a path, whose first forced neighbor creates a claw and then stalls; seeds of size <=2 also stall. Every connected induced four-vertex subgraph is a path, square or claw; claws cannot force. For n>=6 the only squares are rung squares and all induced 4-paths fall into three disjoint types counted 2n,4n,2n. The four representative forcing sequences complete both rims, proving all 9n seeds. Enumerating local replacements of each retained triple yields degree 6 for path types A,B,D and degree 8 for the square type C; handshake yields 28n. A-type translates connect each rim and B/C/D moves join all types and both rims. Independent direct exhaustive four-subset forcing and exchange graph BFS for n=6..12 agreed with vertex counts, edge counts, degrees and connectivity. The unrestricted n statement follows the local classification, not finite tests.
